introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Computer Science 2 (0595), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2019. Duration: two hours.**

Answer any FIVE questions. All questions carry 20 marks each. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators or Phones are NOT allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The technician of a computer laboratory in a school decides to replace a Proprietary Operating system with an Open Source Operating System. He equally replaced the RAM chips with RAM of higher capacities and supplied power to each computers through a UPS.

(i) Briefly explain the advantages of the three changes effected by the technician. (6 marks)

(ii) Briefly explain what you understand by Free and Open Source Software. (3 marks)

(iii) Write in full the abbreviation UPS to the computer system. (1 mark)

(iv) Give two advantage of UPS to the computer system. (2 marks)

(v) Suggest other two changes that can improve the functioning of the computers (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Advantages of the three changes (6 marks, 2 marks for each change).**

1. **Open source operating system instead of a proprietary one:** it is free or much cheaper (no licence fee for each computer); it can be copied to all computers without licence limits; its source code can be adapted to the needs of the school; it is supported by a large community and receives frequent security updates.
2. **RAM of higher capacity:** more programs and larger files can be kept in memory at the same time, so the computers run faster and slow down less (less swapping to the hard disk) and can run several programs together.
3. **Power through a UPS:** the computers keep running for a short time during a power cut and are protected from power surges and voltage drops, so work is not lost and the hardware is not damaged.

**(ii) Free and Open Source Software (3 marks).** Free and Open Source Software (FOSS) is software whose licence gives users the freedom to run it for any purpose, to study and modify it (the source code is available to everybody), to copy it and to share it with others, with or without changes. "Free" refers to freedom, not only to the price. Examples: Linux, LibreOffice, Firefox.

**(iii) UPS (1 mark).** UPS = **Uninterruptible Power Supply**.

**(iv) Two advantages of a UPS (2 marks, 1 mark each).** Any two of: it supplies power from its battery when the mains fails, so the user has time to save work and shut down properly; it protects the computer from power surges and spikes; it prevents loss of data and damage to the hardware; some models also regulate the voltage.

**(v) Two other changes (2 marks, 1 mark each).** Any two of: install an up-to-date antivirus and a firewall; replace the hard disk drives with faster solid state drives (or add storage); upgrade the processor; keep the software up to date; install good ventilation or air conditioning and keep the machines dust-free.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Briefly explain the following:

(i) Multitasking and multiprocessing. (2 marks)

(ii) Software upgrading and updating. (2 marks)

(iii) Uploading and downloading. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Multitasking and multiprocessing (2 marks).**

- **Multitasking:** the operating system lets one computer run several programs (tasks) at the same time on one processor by switching quickly between them (time slicing). Example: typing a document while music plays.
- **Multiprocessing:** the computer has two or more processors (or cores) that execute several processes truly at the same time, which increases the processing speed.

**(ii) Software upgrading and updating (2 marks).**

- **Upgrading:** replacing the software with a newer, more advanced version that has major new features (usually a new version number).
- **Updating:** installing small changes (patches) to the version already installed, to fix errors, close security holes or refresh data such as the virus definitions of an antivirus.

**(iii) Uploading and downloading (2 marks).**

- **Uploading:** sending a file from your own computer to another computer or to a server on a network or the Internet (for example posting a photo on a website or attaching a file to an email).
- **Downloading:** receiving or copying a file from a remote computer or server to your own computer.
